`binaryRL` is built upon the foundational four-step framework (Wilson & Collins, [2019](https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.49547)) for computational modeling. This provides a systematic roadmap that ensures methodological rigor throughout the entire process, from model construction to result reporting. To facilitate immediate use, the package includes three pre-built, canonical reinforcement learning models as described by Niv et al. [(2012)](https://doi.org/10.1523/JNEUROSCI.5498-10.2012).

<img src="./fig/2026_TutorialRL/rl_process.png" alt="RL Process" width="34.25%" style="display: inline;"/> <img src="./fig/2026_TutorialRL/rl_models.png" alt="RL Models" width="61%" style="display: inline;"/>

</p>

Researchers need only understand the interaction between the core components of a Markov Decision Process (MDP) to begin building their own tailored models. By utilizing familiar `if-else` logic to define custom cognitive processes, users can bypass the steep learning curve traditionally associated with coding reinforcement learning from scratch. The entire modeling workflow is streamlined into four key functions: `run_m()` for core model execution, `rcv_d()` for parameter and model recovery, `fit_p()` for fitting real data, and `rpl_e()` for replaying experimental effects.
